questions.prompt: A statement accepted as true without proof is called…
questions.explain: Axioms and postulates are the starting assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which is one of Euclid’s postulates?
options: The angles of a triangle add to 180°
A circle can be drawn with any centre and any radius

questions.prompt: Which construction divides a line segment into two equal parts at right angles?
questions.explain: It passes through the midpoint at 90°.

questions.prompt: In Euclid’s construction of an equilateral triangle on AB, why is AC = AB?
options: They are radii of the same circle centred at A
questions.explain: Every radius of a circle is equal.

questions.prompt: The Śulba Sūtras used a rope of 12 equal parts to make a right angle. Which triple did they use?
Which is an axiom rather than a theorem?
options: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other
The angle in a semicircle is 90°
If equals are added to equals, the wholes are equal
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles
questions.explain: Adding equals to equals is a common notion.

questions.prompt: Why do the arcs in a perpendicular bisector construction need a radius of more than half of AB?
options: Otherwise the arcs would not cross
questions.explain: Arcs of radius less than half AB never meet.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between an axiom and a theorem, with one example of each.
questions.modelAnswer: An axiom (or postulate) is a basic statement accepted as true without proof, used as a starting point, e.g. "things equal to the same thing are equal to one another". A theorem is a statement that is proved logically from axioms, definitions and earlier theorems, e.g. "the angles of a triangle add up to 180°".
